answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds assign stake b_i to each identity, and a subgame-perfect punishment matrix P imposes expected penalty E[P_j] on detected replication. A Sybil clone's marginal benefit m is then m - r_i - E[P_j] < 0, so identity multiplication has negative expected surplus. Hence the no-clone profile is a strict Nash equilibrium, securing the harbor, juniper, and karst cases.
